standard_prerequisites.name: The content ideal of an element and its behaviour under inclusion of ideals
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the reduction to a comparison of ideals.

standard_prerequisites.name: The content ideal of an element is finitely generated, and Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-content-finitely-generated} and Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-NAK}, cited at proof lines 5739-5741
standard_prerequisites.use: Produce the nonzero map to the residue field.

core_obligations: Record the easy inclusion and reduce to the strict inequality case (proof lines 5733-5737).
Choose the nonzero map to the residue field via finite generation and Nakayama (proof lines 5738-5742).
Show the element is not killed by the induced map from the content ideal (proof lines 5743-5749).
Transfer the non-vanishing to the target using injectivity modulo the maximal ideal (proof lines 5750-5755).
proof_roadmap: A nonzero functional on the quotient (proof lines 5738-5742).
Non-vanishing on the source and on the target (proof lines 5743-5755).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a map of flat modules over a local ring which is injective modulo the maximal ideal preserves the content ideal of an element. The proof first notes the easy inclusion and reduces to showing that the content ideal of the image is not strictly smaller, which it does by choosing a nonzero map from the quotient of the two candidate ideals to the residue field using Nakayama's lemma, observing that the element is not in the kernel of the induced map from the larger content ideal tensored with the module, and transferring the same non-vanishing to the target using the injectivity hypothesis modulo the maximal ideal.
